claims.quote: there is a small bit of anger, I would say, I would feel if those pilots are still facing that difficulty in reporting this topic and they do not have the tools to be able to mitigate this issue.

claims.v: commercial pilots are seeing similar objects, typically closer, with less range and fewer sensors
claims.quote: Commercial pilots are seeing them and they are typically closer and the range of what they are seeing is pretty large.

claims.v: he would absolutely not have been able to defend himself, crew or aircraft had the encounters become hostile
claims.quote: would you have had the capability to defend yourself, your crew, your aircraft? Mr. Graves. Absolutely not.

claims.v: came forward because colleagues had no way to mitigate the safety threat
claims.quote: I came forward because I felt that my colleagues did not have a way to mitigate the safety threat and I wanted to help them.

claims.v: there are few public options for reporting; even professionals with sensor data are hesitant to come forward
claims.quote: Right now I do not think there is a lot of public options for the everyman to be able to report on this.

claims.v: he was an operator who depended on people like Grusch to do the homework
claims.quote: I was an operator, so I was depending on folks like Mr. Grusch to do that homework.

claims.v: objects with no wings, no IR energy and no tether were primarily what they were experiencing
claims.quote: Nothing tethering it to the ground, and that was primarily what we were experiencing out there.

claims.v: has no answer on whether there is an active disinformation campaign
claims.quote: Mr. Graves. I do not have an answer to that.

claims.v: operator (pilot); trained as an aviation safety officer by the Navy
claims.quote: I was trained as an aviation safety officer by the Navy and this seemed--it just felt right.

claims.v: Commander
claims.quote: Commander Fravor, can you briefly describe your background?

claims.v: naval aviator
claims.quote: As an expert naval aviator have you ever seen an object that looked and moved like the Tic Tac UAP?

claims.v: enlisted Marine, Naval Academy graduate, flew in the Navy for 18 years, Master's from University of Houston, then private sector defense work
claims.quote: I was an enlisted Marine, Naval Academy graduate, Navy, flew for 18 years. Got a Master's from University of Houston and I have worked in the private sector for the last what now, 19--16 years, 17 years. I do a lot of defense work.

claims.v: accident investigator
claims.quote: For me, you know, I was an accident investigator.

claims.v: you have to know where to look and who to talk to; Grusch can point Congress there
claims.quote: But if you know where to look and who to talk to, which is exactly where Mr. Grusch can point you then you have them.

claims.v: as a user of training ranges: reports are made but no one collects the radar data to back them up
claims.quote: Right now, you get the report. Someone says, I saw something, but no one collects the radar data to back it up and do research.

claims.v: things are over-classified; once classified they go in a vault
claims.quote: So, they are over classified, and as soon as they do that they go in a vault and then you all have to look for them.

claims.v: faced no repercussions from superiors for reporting
claims.quote: Mr. Graves. No. Commander Fravor. No.

claims.v: there was disinformation previously, as with Project Bluebook; cannot speak for the government currently
claims.quote: Commander Fravor. Previously with, like, Project Bluebook, yes, but currently I do not speak for the U.S. Government.

claims.v: had never seen an object that looked and moved like the Tic Tac
claims.quote: have you ever seen an object that looked and moved like the Tic Tac UAP? Commander Fravor. No.

claims.v: the government does not test advanced weapons next to its jets without informing pilots; there are test ranges for that
claims.quote: Commander Fravor. No. We have test ranges for that.

claims.v: has never seen a propulsion system that creates no thermal exhaust
claims.quote: In your career have you ever seen a propulsion system that creates no thermal exhaust? Commander Fravor. No.

claims.v: the fastest plane on Earth could not do the maneuvers he saw
claims.quote: would it be capable of doing that? Commander Fravor. No, not even close.

claims.v: the 2004 encounter was his first UFO or UAP encounter and he has had none since
claims.quote: I wonder was this the first time that you encountered a UFO or a UAP in 2004? Commander Fravor. Yes.

claims.v: never felt we were alone, but was not a UFO person
claims.quote: I never felt that we were alone with all the planets out there. But I was not a UFO person.

claims.v: what they experienced was well beyond material science and capabilities then, now, or in the next 10 to 20 years
claims.quote: well beyond the material science and the capabilities that we had at the time, that we have currently, or that we are going to have in the next 10 to 20 years.

claims.v: came forward after being pestered by a friend who said he would add credibility to the New York Times article
claims.quote: I was pestered by a friend, and I asked why and he said, you are the one person that they cannot discredit, and you will add credibility to the New York Times article.

claims.v: advice to witnesses: stick to the facts, write it down and do not speculate
claims.quote: Write it down and do not speculate what you think it is because it will sway your decision. Just write the facts down.

claims.v: UAPs are definitely potentially an existential threat to national security
claims.quote: Commander Fravor. Same answer, potentially. I would say definitely potentially.

claims.v: the world needs to know it is not a joke
claims.quote: I would say the world needs to know that. It is not a joke.

claims.v: does not know whether the Department of Energy is involved in UAP data collection
claims.quote: Mr. Ogles. Mr. Fravor? Commander Fravor. No, I do not know.

claims.v: was told the Department of Defense has maybe 60 percent of its assets unaccounted for
claims.quote: I was told the Department of Defense maybe 60 percent of their assets are unaccounted for, whatever the heck that means.

claims.v: has been in Congress 5 years
claims.quote: we audit the Pentagon every year and I have been here 5 years and they fail the daggum thing every year.

claims.v: has heard people talk about Havana syndrome type incidences in connection with injuries
claims.quote: I have heard people talk about Havana syndrome type incidences.

claims.v: thanked people all over the world who kept the issue alive despite criticism
claims.quote: people all over the world that have kept this issue alive.

claims.v: there is nothing above Special Access Program classification, so being denied access defies congressional practice
claims.quote: the notion that we are not being given that access sort of defies our typical muscle memory here in Congress.

claims.v: Congress needs to meet Grusch in a secure compartmentalized facility
claims.quote: Every person watching this knows that we need to meet with Mr. Grusch in a secure compartmentalized facility so that we can get fulsome answers that do not put him in jeopardy

claims.v: the reporting culture, in which UAP reports carry perceived career consequences, must change
claims.quote: does have a perceived consequence to these people and that is a culture we must change if we want to get to the truth.

claims.v: the committee is one for whistleblowers and their protection
claims.quote: this is a committee for whistleblowers and for the protection of whistleblowers as well.

claims.v: defense contractors have abused their contracts and notification requirements to Congress have been abused
claims.quote: we have seen defense contractors abuse their contracts before through this Committee.

claims.v: his state has two very large training ranges; asks what Congress can do about UAP impacts on them
claims.quote: what steps can Congress take to address training range impacts? And I say that having two very large training rages in my state.

claims.v: has been in Congress for 6 months and is pretty skeptical
claims.quote: Look, I have been here for 6 months and I am pretty skeptical.

claims.v: finds it far-fetched that an advanced species could travel billions of light years and then crash on Earth
claims.quote: somehow is incompetent enough to not survive Earth or crashes is something that I find a little bit farfetched.

claims.v: asked whether recovered craft could be the product of domestic military contractors (Occam's Razor)
claims.quote: Occam's Razor is that this--these aircrafts have they been identified that they are being produced by domestic, you know, military contractors?

claims.v: many dismiss UAP reports as classified weapons testing by the US government
claims.quote: Many dismiss UAP reports as classified weapons testing by our own government.

claims.v: unknown objects could be UAPs, weather phenomena, advanced technology of allied or enemy forces, or something out of this world
claims.quote: Whether these are UAPs or weather phenomena, advanced technology from American allied or enemy forces, or something more out of this world.

claims.v: either the United States has an unknown adversary or there are serious investigations to do
claims.quote: either the United States has an adversary here in this world that we do not know or we really have some serious investigations to do.

claims.v: there clearly is a threat to US national security; will invoke the Holman Rule against anyone denying Congress access
claims.quote: if that access is denied I will personally volunteer to initiate the Holman Rule against any personnel or any program or any agency that denies access to Congress.

claims.v: Grusch mentioned white collar crimes potentially taking place in regard to a cover up
claims.quote: you mentioned white collar crimes potentially being--taking place in regards to a cover up.

claims.v: asked whether safety measures exist with foreign governments to avoid escalation if a malevolent UAP event occurs
claims.quote: are their safety measures in place with foreign governments or other superpowers to avoid an escalatory situation in the event that a UAP malevolent event occurs?

claims.v: asked Fravor whether 2004 was his first UFO or UAP encounter and Graves about commercial pilots' sightings
claims.quote: Are there also commercial pilots who have encountered the same kind of sightings that you described before?
